title: CTM-UNet: Integrating Convolutional Tsetlin Machines with U-Net Architecture for Semantic Segmentation
venue: 2025 International Symposium on the Tsetlin Machine (ISTM), IEEE
new_feature: CTM-UNet: a U-Net encoder-decoder whose convolutional blocks are replaced by (conv preprocessing + binarization + CTM2D) blocks producing integer votes cast to float, with per-class CTM heads trained by one-vs-rest Type I/II feedback; hybrid with PyTorch tensors.

datasets.name_in_paper: CamVid (32 classes merged to binary Sky vs Background)
datasets.input_shape_or_features: RGB resized to 512x512; each 8-bit channel value expanded to 8 binary bits -> 512x512x24
datasets.split_as_reported: training set 367 images (80% of available training data), validation 92 images (20%), independent test set 233 images (as stated; numbers inconsistent with 701 total and with the standard 367/101/233 CamVid split)
datasets.booleanization: 8-bit binary expansion of each RGB value (H x W x 3 -> H x W x 24); multi-threshold binarization inside CTM blocks
datasets.notes: Original 701 images with 32 classes; experiments merge all classes into Sky (foreground) vs other (background). Data augmentation: random rotation, brightness/saturation/hue.

extraction_notes: Only the binary Sky-vs-background experiment has quantitative results (Table I); no 32-class mIoU is reported despite the abstract/conclusion wording. UNet baseline at 99.99% acc/IoU looks implausible but is as printed. Split numbers as stated are internally inconsistent (367 described as 80% of training data; 367+92+233=692 vs 701). Memory figures are analytical (bit width), not measured. Category 'segmentation'.
caution: Only a binary sky-vs-background task on CamVid is reported (not 32-class segmentation); the stated split does not add up and memory figures are analytical estimates.
